_disclaimer: Personal research notes for situational awareness — not legal advice, not dating advice. Laws, scenes, and risk patterns change. Verify with official sources and local knowledge before you travel or act.

Scotland.lgbt_climate: Same-sex marriage legal (UK). Glasgow and Edinburgh have visible queer nightlife; smaller towns quieter. Bi travelers usually navigate both queer and mixed scenes without legal issues.
Scotland.gay_scene: Apps (Grindr etc.) active in cities; pubs/clubs in Glasgow Merchant City and Edinburgh. Meet in public first; late-night venues can be rowdy but not uniquely dangerous vs other UK cities.
Scotland.straight_scene: Pubs and clubs in city centres; tourist-heavy Edinburgh. Same drink-spiking awareness as elsewhere in the UK.
Scotland.bring_someone_back: Most hotels allow adult guests; some budget hostels restrict overnight visitors — ask desk. Airbnb: check house rules and respect hosts. UK hotels may ask guests to sign in.
hookup_scams: Theft after inviting someone to a room (phone/wallet left out).
Drink spiking in busy clubs — watch your glass.
Fake profiles pushing you to a private flat quickly.
common_scams: Distraction theft in crowded tourist streets (Royal Mile).
Overpriced or cash-only unofficial tours — book named operators.
Scotland.street_crime: Pickpocketing in tourist hubs. Knife crime exists in parts of Glasgow as a broader UK urban issue — avoid unknown late-night confrontations; stick to well-lit areas. Guns are rare vs US norms.
stay_safe: Share live location with a friend when meeting someone new.
Meet in a public bar first; keep valuables off the bed/counter.
Use licensed taxis or major ride apps late at night.

Ireland.lgbt_climate: Marriage equality since 2015. Dublin has a clear queer scene; Cork smaller but present. Generally socially accepting in cities.
Ireland.gay_scene: Dublin apps + known gay bars; smaller cities quieter. Public meetups preferred.
Ireland.straight_scene: Temple Bar is tourist-heavy — fun but pickpocket and overcharging risk. Prefer neighbourhood pubs for lower scam density.
Ireland.bring_someone_back: Hotels usually fine with adult guests; hostels vary. Airbnb: follow listing rules. Don't assume shared rooms allow overnight guests.
hookup_scams: Room theft after a meet.
Spiked drinks in busy Temple Bar venues.
Pressure to move to an unknown private address immediately.
common_scams: Pickpockets in Temple Bar and on packed Luas/buses.
Ireland.street_crime: Mostly opportunistic theft. Serious violence uncommon for tourists who avoid fights; stay aware after pubs close.
stay_safe: Keep bags zipped and phones pocketed in crowds.
Meet publicly; tell someone your plans.

England.lgbt_climate: Legal protections strong; London/Manchester/Brighton major scenes. Bi travelers commonly use both queer and mixed apps/venues.
England.gay_scene: London (Soho, Vauxhall, etc.), Manchester Canal Street, Brighton. Apps everywhere in cities.
England.straight_scene: Large nightlife economy; tourist zones (West End, city centres) have higher theft and spiking awareness needs.
England.bring_someone_back: Hotels typically allow registered adult guests; some require ID at desk. Many Airbnbs forbid parties/extra guests — read the house rules before inviting anyone.
hookup_scams: Classic 'come to my place' robbery setups — meet public first.
Drink spiking.
Phone theft during intimacy; keep bag in bathroom or locked.
Romance/advance-fee variants less common in-person but fake profiles exist.
common_scams: Pickpockets on Tube, at stations, and major sights.
England.street_crime: Pickpocketing is the main tourist risk. Knife crime is a real urban issue in some boroughs — don't engage street confrontations; leave. Firearms rare relative to US.
stay_safe: Mind the gap — and your phone on open-pocket Tube rides.
Use TfL / licensed black cabs / major apps at night.

Wales.lgbt_climate: UK law; Cardiff has the main scene. Smaller towns quieter.
Wales.gay_scene: Cardiff apps/venues; elsewhere limited — plan around cities.
Wales.straight_scene: Pub culture; Cardiff nightlife similar to other mid-size UK cities.
Wales.bring_someone_back: Same UK hotel/Airbnb pattern — ask if unsure; respect hostel rules.
hookup_scams: Room theft.
Isolated meets away from city centres — prefer public first.
common_scams: Rural hiking: less scam risk, more weather/navigation risk.
Wales.street_crime: Lower tourist density than London; still use normal city caution at night.

Northern Ireland.lgbt_climate: Marriage equality later than the rest of UK (2020). Belfast scene exists; be more discreet in some smaller towns.
Northern Ireland.gay_scene: Belfast apps and a smaller venue scene than Dublin/London.
Northern Ireland.straight_scene: Pubs/clubs in Belfast; normal nightlife caution.
Northern Ireland.bring_someone_back: Hotels generally OK; confirm hostel/Airbnb guest rules.
hookup_scams: Room theft.
Spiking awareness in busy venues.
common_scams: Avoid political provocation — tourism is fine, street arguments are not.
Northern Ireland.street_crime: Mostly ordinary urban theft risks. Be aware of local tensions in specific areas; stick to well-trafficked tourist/nightlife districts at night.

France.lgbt_climate: Marriage equality; Paris has a large queer scene; cities generally fine. Rural areas vary in social openness.
France.gay_scene: Paris (Marais etc.) very active; Lyon/Marseille present. Apps widely used.
France.straight_scene: Dense nightlife in cities; tourist zones (around major sights) have higher scam density.
France.bring_someone_back: Hotels usually allow adult guests; some require ID for all overnight visitors (common in France). Airbnb: house rules bind — unauthorized guests can get you kicked out.
hookup_scams: Theft in the room.
Drink spiking.
Aggressive 'friendly' strangers steering you to bars with inflated bills (more classic tourist scam adjacent to nightlife).
common_scams: Petition / bracelet / gold-ring distraction scams near Louvre, Eiffel, Montmartre.
Pickpockets on Métro line 1 and RER to airports.
Fake police ID checks asking to see wallets — real police won't ask you to hand over your wallet casually; ask for a station.
France.street_crime: Pickpocketing is the #1 tourist issue. Violent street crime against tourists is uncommon but not zero — avoid empty corridors late; keep bags cross-body.

Spain.lgbt_climate: Strong legal protections; Madrid and Barcelona among Europe's most visible queer scenes. Bi travelers usually fine in cities.
Spain.gay_scene: Chueca (Madrid), Gaixample (Barcelona), Sitges nearby. Apps very active.
Spain.straight_scene: Huge nightlife; Las Ramblas / Plaza Mayor tourist zones = pickpocket magnets.
Spain.bring_someone_back: Hotels generally allow guests; some ask for ID. Many tourist flats (Airbnb) ban extra guests — check rules. Don't leave doors propped in shared buildings.
hookup_scams: Room theft (very common pattern worldwide).
Spiking.
Robbery setups via apps — public meetup non-negotiable.
Someone 'helping' with a spilled drink / mustard distraction while an accomplice steals.
common_scams: Pickpockets on Las Ramblas, Metro, beaches.
Spain.street_crime: Pickpocketing is endemic in top tourist corridors. Violent muggings less common but happen at night in isolated spots — stick to busy streets; don't follow strangers to ATMs.
stay_safe: Beach: use hotel safe; don't leave phones under towels.

Portugal.lgbt_climate: Legal equality; Lisbon and Porto have active scenes. Generally relaxed in cities.
Portugal.gay_scene: Lisbon Príncipe Real area and apps; Porto smaller.
Portugal.straight_scene: Bairro Alto / Cais do Sodré nightlife; tourist denser = higher theft awareness.
Portugal.bring_someone_back: Hotels usually OK; Airbnb guest rules vary — confirm. Older buildings: be mindful of building entry norms.
hookup_scams: Room theft.
Spiking in busy bars.
App meets that push immediately to isolated viewpoints at night — prefer busy areas.
common_scams: Pickpockets on trams (esp. 28) and in Alfama crowds.
Portugal.street_crime: Mostly opportunistic theft. Violent crime against tourists is relatively low; still use normal night caution in empty streets.
